newsitem.title: FINLAND: Partek to buy Swedish Kalmar.
newsitem.headline: Partek to buy Swedish Kalmar.

text.p: Finnish cargo handling and building materials group Partek said on Tuesday it would buy 51 percent of Swedish vehicles maker Kalmar Industries.
The merger would generate synergies of 65 million to 100 million markka per year, Partek said in a statement.
The companies had signed a letter of intent on the deal which was subject to approval from anti-trust bodies, it said.
"As a result of the merger, Partek will become an owner of Kalmar with a 51 percent shareholding, which will make Kalmar a Partek subsidiary," it said.
"Kalmar's quotation on the Stockholm Stock Exchange will continue," it added.
The proposed merger between Kalmar and Sisu Terminal Systems (STS), a Partek subsidiary, would create "the world's leading company in container-handling machines," it said.
The company's net sales would be 3.1 billion markka and the workforce would number some 3,200, Partek added.
Kalmar will acquire STS via a rights issue targeted at Partek.

Kalmar's board of directors will propose that about 250 million Swedish crowns be paid to current shareholders through a shares redemption in the autumn of 1997. Every tenth share would be redeemed at a price of 200 crowns each, Partek said.

"After the redemption has been implemented, the share issue (to Partek of approximately 12 million shares) will be the equivalent of 51 percent of Kalmar's shares and voting rights," it said, adding the new shares would entitle to full dividend for 1997.
After the redemption of shares and the share issue, the number of Kalmar shares was expected to rise to 23.5 million, Partek said.
The nominal value of each share is 12.50 crowns and so the share capital after the redemption and the share issue would be about 294 million crowns.
"The combined equity capital of the new group will be over one billion Swedish crowns, and the amount of capital employed will be about 1.9 billion crowns following the merger," it said.
